title: Counting the Days of Cover Bought on a Released Policy
content:
The days of cover bought on a policy of the Travel Protection Plans, when cover is given up, are counted
from a day that depends on whether the certificate was issued before the journey began, and on whether the
journey has ended.

## The three readings

1. Where the certificate was issued before the first date of the journey, the days of cover bought are counted
   from the day the certificate was issued to the last date of the journey, both counted, because cover against
   cancellation runs from the moment the certificate is issued.
2. Where the certificate was issued on or after the first date of the journey and the journey has not ended,
   they are counted from the day the certificate was issued to the last date of the journey, that last date
   counted.
3. In every other case the days of cover bought are the days of the journey, its first and last both counted.

## The counts compared on hypothetical dates

A journey runs from the 10th to the 19th. A certificate issued on the 1st gives 19 days under the first reading,
the 1st and the 19th both counted. A certificate issued on the 12th, the journey not having ended, gives 7 days
under the second, the 19th counted and the 12th not. A certificate issued on the 12th of a journey that has
already ended gives 10 days under the third, the 10th and the 19th both counted.
